This misc. appeal by the appellants/claimants u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the Award dated 04.08.2022 passed by Fourth Member, Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dabra District- Gwalior (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.10 of 2020 whereby the Claims Tribunal has rejected the claim petition filed by the appellants.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 21.09.2019, Hariram Yadav who was working as Head Constable in Police Department posted at Kampoo, District- Gwalior and was on duty, going on his motorcycle bearing Registration No.MP 07 ND 2008 for the purpose of investigation and serving warrant to someone, met with an accident with a loading truck TATA 407 bearing Registration No. MP 32 G 0481 near village- Jangipura at Biloua- Picchore Road.

First Information Report (Ex.P-2) under section 154 CrPC was lodged by Satyendra Singh Yadav, son of the deceased- Hariram Yadav at Police Station- Picchore, District Gwalior on 01.10.2019 after submitting a written complaint to police station -Picchore (Ex.P-3).

sentences.text: After completion of investigation and other formalities, charge- sheet was filed against the offending vehicle.
Appellants being legal representatives filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation.
3. On being noticed, respondents appeared before the Claims Tribunal and filed their written statement.

Learned Claims Tribunal, after taking evidence of both the parties and after hearing the rival parties, rejected the claim petition filed by the claimants on the ground that the claimants have failed to prove that alleged accident was caused by the offending vehicle.

4. Being dissatisfied with the impugned Award, the appellants has filed this appeal with submissions that the the Claims Tribunal rejected the claim petition of the appellants without going through material and evidence available on record and the finding recorded by the Claims Tribunal that the accident was not caused by the offending vehicle, is contrary to law.

Appellants had examined eye-witness - Devendra (AW-3), who in his evidence, has categorically stated that the accident was occurred by the offending vehicle but the Claims Tribunal has discarded the evidence of this witness although he is not a family member of deceased and he is not an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 3 MA-5343-2022 interested witness.

It is further contended that the owner of the offending vehicle accepted as per provisions of Section 133 of the Motor Vehicles Act that the alleged accident was occurred by his offending vehicle, therefore, the Claims Tribunal has committed error in disbelieving the acceptance/admission given by the owner of the offending vehicle.
Delay in lodging the FIR has properly been explained.
Therefore, the finding of the Claims Tribunal is erroneous, liable to be set aside and it is prayed that a just and reasonable amount of compensation be awarded in favour of claimants.

In support of his contentions, learned Counsel for the appellants has relied on Coordinate Bench decision of this Court in the case of Smt. Kusum and Others vs. Kalu alias Kaluram and Another (MA No. 1867 of 2016, decided on 18th of January,
2024).

6. Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.

It is true that if the claimant has been able to demonstrate NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 4 MA-5343-2022 satisfactory and cogent reason for delay in lodging the F.I.R. then delay in lodging F.I.R. should not be treated as fatal for such proceeding.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226 in para 20 and 21 has held as under:-

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case. Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."

8. According to Ex.P-10, an information was given on the basis of Rojmamcha Sanha by Shri Vinay Kumar Sharma, Inspector to the family member of deceased Hariram Yadav, who had met with an accident and was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 5 MA-5343-2022 admitted in JA Hospital, Gwalior.
In Ex.P-10, there was neither any registration number nor the nature of offending vehicle was mentioned.

9. Requisition form for conduction of Postmortem of deceased vide Exhibit P-6 is reproduced as under:-
"
Age 56
M / CY
: P.M.

P.M.     "

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P-6 dated 25.09.2019, it was mentioned that the accident occurred by any unknown vehicle, due to which Hariram Yadav died during treatment in AIIMS, New Delhi on 25.09.2019.

11. Medical document of AIIMS, New Delhi vide Exhibit P-13 dated 22.09.2019 is reproduced as under:-
"PT BROUGHT BY SAN WITH A/H/O RTA (TWO WHEELER BY UNKNOWN VEHICLE) NEAR GWALIOR, MP THEN PT WAS SHIFTED TO RUN APOLLO SPECTRA HOSPITALS, GWALIOR WHEE INITIAL MANAGEMENT WAS DONE THEN PT WAS SHIFTED TO JPNATC AIIMS FOR FURTHER MNAGEMENTB BY SON IN AMBULANCE WITH ENDOTRACHEAL TUBE, FOLEYS CATHETER,
RYLES TUBE AND CANNULA IN SITU."

12. It is also clear that neither registration number of offending vehicle nor the nature/type of offending vehicle was mentioned in the above mentioned document Ex.P-13.
13.

In the present case, it appears that on 25.09.2019, Hariram Yadav died and then on 01.10.2019 son of deceased Satyendra Singh filed a written complaint with registration number of offending vehicle and nature of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 6 MA-5343-2022 offending of offending vehicle, on the basis of which an FIR was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle.
On perusal of evidence of AW-1 Shanti Devi and AW-2 - Satyendra Singh Yadav, it is clear that these witnesses are not eye-witnesses.
According to Ex.P-3 which is a written complaint filed by AW-2- Satyendra Singh Yadav, the accident was seen by Devendra Parihar, Shishupal Singh and Jitendra Yadav.
Then, they informed by mobile to Birendra Singh Yadav, uncle of Satyendra Singh Yadav, who thereafter informed the incident to Satyendra, son of deceased on mobile.

Thereafter, they reached the spot and took Hariram Yadav for treatment to JA Hospital, Gwalior,
from where he was referred to Apollo Hospital, Gwalior.

14. From the written complaint filed by AW-2- Satyendra Singh Yadav, it shows that at the time of the alleged accident, the registration number and nature of vehicle was known and the accident was seen by Devendra Parihar, Shishupal Singh and Jitendra Yadav, who informed the family member of deceased- Hariram Yadav.
Therefore, Devendra Parihar appears to be a star witness and examined as eye-witness.

Devendra Parihar in his chief examination deposed that on 21.09.2019 at 3:00 PM,
while Hariram Yadav was going on his motorcycle bearing Registration No.MP 07 ND 2008, at that time, the offending vehicle bearing Registration No.MP 32 G 0481 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle of Hariram and thereafter, driver of the offending vehicle ran away from the spot.
The alleged accident was seen by Devendra Parihar, Shishupal Singh and Jitendra Yadav.

Devendra (AW-3) who is alleged to be an eye-witness, NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 7 MA-5343-2022 in his chief-examination, stated that he does not know Hariram Yadav and also does not know Shanti Devi and Satyendra Singh Yadav before the alleged accident and in para 10 of his cross-examination, he further deposed that it is wrong to say that Satyendra, son of deceased had given him documents Ex.P-31 to P-48 (treatment documents of Hariram and identity related documents) before his statement, but these documents Ex.P-31 to Satyendra Singh Yadav vs Shriram General Insurance Company ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32818166/
4 Ex.P-48 were filed by him before the Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: So, if a witness does not know the deceased and family members of the deceased before the alleged accident, then as to why he had filed these documents Ex.P-31 to P- 48 during statement, which shows that Devendra is an interested witness in the case.
15. Devendra Parihar who is allegedly to be an eye-witness of accident has not stated anything before the police and nor any report was made by him.

Although this witness stated that he has given the information regarding alleged accident to the brother of deceased -Birendra Singh Yadav,
who thereafter informed the incident to Satyendra Singh who is son of the deceased, but neither Birendra Singh nor Satyendra Singh gave any information regarding registration number of offending vehicle to the police or in hospital.
16.

It is settled principle of law that if police registered a case against the offending vehicle and after investigation, filed the charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, then the Claims Tribunal shall presume the guilty of driver of the offending vehicle

. It is also settled principle of law that mere delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the case of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 8 MA-5343-2022 claimants, but this presumption is rebuttable in evidence.

A person who claimed that the accident was not occurred by the offending vehicle, then burden always lies upon him to rebut the presumption by way of adducing direct or oral evidence adduced by the claimants.
17. In the present case, AW-2 Satyendra Singh who is the son of deceased filed a complaint on 01.10.2019, after nine days of alleged accident and after five days of death of deceased.

So, it is the duty of son of deceased- Satyendra Singh (AW-2) to explain as to why he has not lodged the complaint promptly and as to why he has filed the complaint before the police after five days of death of deceased.
It was also the duty of brother of deceased, Birendra Singh Yadav who knew the registration number of offending vehicle, but this witness has also not given any information to police in this regard.

18. Devendra (AW-3) in his examination in chief, stated that he did not know the deceased and his family members before the accident, but this witness filed documents Ex.P-31 to Ex.P-48 relating to treatment of deceased and the documents regarding identification of appellants before the Claims Tribunal at the time of recording his evidence which shows his eagerness about proving the accident.

He had no dare to lodge the FIR against the driver of the offending vehicle as he has already stated that he had seen the alleged accident and knew the registration number of offending vehicle, but he has not given any information regarding registration number of offending vehicle to the police authorities, therefore, his evidence appears to be doubtful and not trustworthy.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 9 MA-5343-2022 19.

If Satyendra Singh (AW-2) knew the registration number of offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident, then why he has not given any information to JA Hospital, where his father was firstly admitted for treatment.
He has also not given any information to AIIMS, New Delhi, where his father/deceased was referred for treatment.

As per Ex.P-13, it was informed in AIIMS Hospital Satyendra Singh Yadav vs Shriram General Insurance Company ... on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32818166/
5 that an unknown vehicle dashed the motorcycle of deceased.

entities.text: AIIMS Hospital Satyendra Singh Yadav vs Shriram General Insurance Company
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
From the evidence of Satyendra Singh Yadav (AW-2) who is son of the deceased, it appears that if he had known registration number of offending vehicle at the time of alleged accident, but would have no dare to give information in this regard till 01.10.2019.
20.

So, considering the evidence of Satyendra Singh Yadav, Devendra Parihar and Birendra as well as documents Ex.P-13 and Ex.P-6, it is found that statements made by Satyendra and Devendra are dubious in nature and full of omissions and contradictions, therefore, the Claims Tribunal has rightly disbelieved the evidence of Satyendra and Devendra.

Only on the basis of challan paper filed by the police and admitting the factum of the accident by the owner of the offending vehicle,
accident of the offending vehicle cannot be accepted until and unless the same is proved by cogent,
substantial and oral evidence.

21. In view of foregoing reasons and discussions, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal has rightly disbelieved the evidence of the Satyendra Singh Yadav (AW-2) and Devendra Parihar (AW- 3) and rightly held that the accident was not occurred by the driver of offending vehicle.

No illegality, infirmity, irregularity or perversity is found NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:20687 10 MA-5343-2022 in the impugned Award passed by the Claims Tribunal,
warranting any interference by this Court.
The Award dated 04.08.2022 passed by Claims Tribunal in Claim Case No.10 of 2020 is hereby affirmed.
22. Appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*
